subject: Order Form — invoicing entity split & PO / tax routing
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@talentgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@talentgrid.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form question — invoicing entity split and VAT

Hi Karthik,

We're finalizing the purchase order on our side but Legal/Finance have one last ask: TalentGrid will pay from two different entities this fiscal year (US entity + UK entity). Our procurement system needs the invoice to be issued to the paying entity for tax/residency reasons. Can Redwood issue split invoices by entity for the same order form, and will the tax/VAT evidence be handled per-entity?

Also attaching our standard PO template — we need to confirm how the net terms map to a split-payment flow (single order form, multiple remit-to). If this is a change from standard practice, please let me know the commercial or timing implications.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Martinez
Head of Procurement, TalentGrid
Attachment: TG_PO_Template.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@talentgrid.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form question — invoicing entity split and VAT

Hi Sofia — thanks for the note and the PO template. Looping in Kimberly (finance) and Marissa (commercial) plus Lauren (legal) so we can confirm the feasible paths. Quick summary of what we'll check:
- Whether we can support a single order form with multiple invoice remit-to entities (yes/no + needed legal language)
- How net terms apply per-entity (do we need separate payment schedules or can one ledger attach multiple remit-to?)
- Tax/VAT evidence per invoice and any additional paperwork (W-8/W-9 or VAT registration screenshots)

Kimberly / Marissa / Lauren — asked to triage and propose one recommended approach (preferred for Redwood ops) and a fallback if Procurement requires strict PO-match.

Sofia — we'll try to get back by Monday with a clear playbook.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sofia Martinez <sofia@talentgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form question — invoicing entity split and VAT

Thanks Karthik — quick ops note from Finance: we can support split invoicing for the same order number but need the following to be provided up front for each remit-to entity:

1) Legal entity name, billing address, VAT/Tax ID, and remit-to email
2) The exact invoicing percentage or dollar allocation (e.g., 60% US entity / 40% UK entity)
3) A PO that references Redwood's Order Form ID and confirms allocation by line item or percentage

Tax evidence: for the UK entity we'll need VAT registration proof (registration number + a recent VAT certificate). For the US entity, we need a W-9 or tax residency confirmation. If both entities are paying different line items (recommended), this maps cleanly to our AR system and preserves net terms per entity.

If TalentGrid requires us to issue a single invoice and TalentGrid handles internal allocations, we'll need a written confirmation (email acceptable) that TalentGrid assumes tax liabilities/withholding — that route increases audit friction.

I'm attaching a one-page template we use to capture entity allocations and evidence. If Sofia can return it completed we can draft the split invoices and confirm net-terms for each remit-to.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: RGW_Invoice_Allocation_Template.xlsx (excel)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@talentgrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form question — invoicing entity split and VAT

Hi Sofia — following Kimberly's notes, we prepared a small redline to the Order Form to add a clause that explicitly authorizes split invoicing and clarifies net terms per remit-to entity. The redline keeps the overall commercial numbers unchanged but adds:
- A Billing Schedule appendix that lists each remit-to entity, percentage allocation, and net terms (Net 30 for US; Net 60 for UK per your request)
- A tax evidence clause requiring registration docs before first invoice
- A PO-match requirement: each invoice must reference the TalentGrid PO number and the Order Form ID

I'm attaching the redlined Order Form (v3). If that looks ok, we'll have Legal (Lauren) incorporate final wording into the master MSA if needed. If TalentGrid prefers to keep the Order Form unchanged and perform internal allocation, we'll need a short indemnity statement confirming they accept tax/residency liabilities.

Please confirm which path you prefer and return the completed allocation template if you want Redwood to issue split invoices.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal, Commercials — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_TG_v3.pdf (pdf)
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@talentgrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form question — invoicing entity split and VAT

Thanks all — we reviewed internally and would prefer Redwood to issue split invoices (option A). Attached is our signed PO and a completed allocation worksheet showing 70% US / 30% UK and the remit-to details, plus VAT cert for the UK entity. Net terms agreed: US Net 30; UK Net 60.

Next steps from TalentGrid: please confirm final Order Form PDF with the Billing Schedule appendix and an invoice schedule (dates) so our Accounts Payable can expect the first invoice. We'll send the PO formally through Coupa as well.

Attached: TalentGrid_PO_20270531.pdf (pdf).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you need anything else from Legal to avoid hold-ups, flag it here and we'll prioritize.

Regards,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Procurement, TalentGrid
